articles.text:
Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:36 AM
Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
Windward Bio Group has completed its public market debut after pricing an initial public offering at $17 per share and raising $225 million in gross proceeds, including a $50 million concurrent private placement from Sanofi.
The clinical-stage biotechnology company began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 13, 2026 and ended its first day with a market capitalization of approximately $1.69 billion.
Windward sold approximately 10.29 million ordinary shares in the offering.
The Basel, Switzerland-based company was founded in 2024 by serial biotechnology entrepreneur Luca Santarelli, M.D., and his team. Santarelli previously helped build VectivBio and Therachon, both of which were ultimately acquired.
Windward has raised $365 million since its formation, including a $200 million Series A in January 2025 and a $165 million crossover financing in May 2026.
Pivotal bioVenture Partners China has invested in the company through each financing round from its early formation through the public listing.
Windward is developing ultra-long-acting antibody treatments for respiratory and dermatologic diseases including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and atopic dermatitis.
Its lead program, WIN378, is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin.
WIN378 is currently being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 POLARIS-1 asthma study and the Phase 2 SIRIUS COPD trial. The drug is being developed for twice-yearly dosing, compared with the once-every-four-weeks schedule of currently approved treatments in the category.
Windward reported positive interim Phase 2 data in September 2026 supporting twice-yearly dosing of WIN378 in asthma.
Its pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13 that is currently in Phase 1 development.
Global rights outside Greater China and certain Asian markets to both programs were licensed from Chinese biopharmaceutical companies.
Windward plans to use IPO proceeds to support clinical development of WIN378 and WIN027, advance additional bispecific antibody programs and fund working capital and general corporate purposes.
The company expects top-line Phase 2 asthma data for WIN378 in the first half of 2027, Phase 2 COPD data in the second half of 2027 and Phase 3 asthma data in the first half of 2029.

articles.text:
Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:03 PM
Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners
Square Nine Capital has led a $206 million financing for Aline Accounting Partners, supporting debt refinancing, near-term acquisitions and continued expansion of the accounting and professional services platform.
The financing consists of a revolving credit facility, a term loan and a delayed draw term loan facility.
Proceeds refinanced existing indebtedness and provided growth capital for acquisitions. The facilities also support Aline’s broader strategy of investing in talent, technology and additional service capabilities.
Aline was formed in August 2024 through the merger of three firms with established operating histories. Its model combines local accounting and advisory relationships with shared business resources.
Member firms receive support across finance and reporting, information technology, human resources, recruiting, staffing, marketing, growth and mergers and acquisitions.
The organization intends to use those shared capabilities to strengthen collaboration, improve operating efficiency and expand what its teams can provide to clients.
CEO Matt Lender said the financing supports Aline’s long-term strategy and will help incoming firms gain resources to develop their businesses.
Square Nine provides flexible capital to middle-market companies, partnering with founders, owners, management teams and financial sponsors.
Its investments support acquisitions, growth, refinancings, recapitalizations and other strategic transactions across different parts of a company’s capital structure.
The Aline transaction combines funding for immediate balance sheet needs with capacity for additional acquisitions. That structure supports both the existing organization and firms joining its network.
Polsinelli served as legal counsel to Aline. Paul Hastings advised Square Nine.
The financing gives Aline additional resources as it develops a platform built around established accounting practices, local client relationships and centralized support functions. Square Nine’s principals said the arrangement provides flexibility for continued expansion and investment in the organization’s capabilities.
KEY QUOTES
“Aline has built a strong foundation for growth by bringing together established accounting firms and investing in the resources that help them thrive. We are pleased to lead a financing that supports these acquisitions and provides flexibility for continued expansion. We look forward to partnering with Aline team as the organization grows and expands its capabilities.”
Christopher Brown And Griffin Coakley, Principals At Square Nine Capital
“This financing marks an important milestone for Aline. Square Nine understood our business and delivered a financing solution that supports our long-term strategy. We are excited to welcome the new firms to Aline and provide their teams with additional resources to grow, broaden their capabilities and continue delivering exceptional service to their clients.”
Matt Lender, CEO Of Aline Accounting Partners

articles.title: Attorney General Hilgers Announces $183.5 Million Multistate Settlement with Rent-to-Own Finance Company Acima Digital, LLC
articles.snippet: Attorney General Hilgers Announces $183.5 Million Multistate Settlement with Rent-to-Own Finance Company Acima Digital, LLC Central Nebraska Today
articles.text:
Lincoln – Attorney General Mike Hilgers announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC, and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC. The settlement includes $43 million in consumer restitution, $10.5 million to participating states, and $130 million in lease balance reductions. Nebraska will receive more than $292,608.42 in restitution and $593,465.05 in lease forgiveness for Nebraska consumers.
Acima, a rent-to-own financing company that partners with Nebraska retailers, was accused of misleading consumers about the terms and costs of its rental-purchase agreements. Forty-three states alleged that Acima advertised 90-day payoff programs without clearly disclosing that consumers were automatically placed in 12-month agreements and could end up paying twice the advertised cash price. The company also allegedly misrepresented its services as traditional credit, marked up merchandise prices, and made it difficult for consumers to return merchandise and end agreements.
Under the settlement, Acima must improve retail partner training, provide clearer advertising and contract disclosures, stop marking up merchandise prices, allow consumers to return merchandise without obstruction, and properly address delivery, damage, and repair issues. The company also cannot report rental-purchase agreements to the three major credit bureaus for five years.
Consumers eligible for restitution or lease forgiveness do not need to take action. The settlement administrator will contact consumers receiving restitution, while Acima will notify those eligible for lease forgiveness.

[Crypto Dealbook] November funding reaches $181 million; Index Industries leads weekly deals
November crypto venture funding totals $181 million across 21 rounds. Index Industries led weekly deals with a $50 million seed round, while 30-day funding rose despite fewer rounds.
By John Kim
Published Nov 16, 2026, 7:23 AM EST
Save Share
Mentioned assets
ONDO Ondo Data: CryptoRank · TokenPost
Crypto venture funding has reached $181 million in November, with Index Industries securing the week's largest deal through a $50 million seed round. API, payments and artificial intelligence led investment focus.
November funding so far totals $181 million across 21 rounds.
The latest monthly tally covers November through November 15.
October closed with $1.85 billion raised across 52 rounds, compared with $680.50 million across 53 rounds in September.
November 9 Seva Money raised $5 million in a seed round led by Blockwall and Revent, with other investors participating. Lithium recorded a strategic investment from LitVM with the amount undisclosed. River One recorded an M&A transaction involving Securitize, also with the amount undisclosed.
November 10 Index Industries raised $50 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed, alongside other investors. Alta secured $47.50 million in a Series A led by Index Ventures, with other participants. Marble raised $11 million in a seed round led by Polychain Capital, alongside other investors.
November 12 Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B led by Octagon Partners, with other investors participating. Kailash recorded a pre-seed round led by UTXO Management with the amount undisclosed. Spout Finance received a strategic investment from Ondo Finance with the amount undisclosed.
November 13 DI recorded funding from OKX Ventures and other investors. The amount and stage were undisclosed.
Over the latest 30 days, the investment activity index fell 35.0% from the previous month. Round counts declined while total funding increased.
The period recorded 57 investment rounds, down 19.7% month over month. Total funding rose 91.2% to $2.32 billion.
The average round size was in the $3 million to $10 million range. Strategic investment was the most active funding stage, while API was the leading investment focus.
Over the past six months, API accounted for the largest investment share at 29.96%, followed by payments at 21.59%, artificial intelligence at 19.82%, RWA at 15.42% and developer tools at 13.22%.
Coinbase Ventures led investor activity over the same period with 29 deals, followed by YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) with 28, a16z Frontier and SBI Holdings with 11 each, Circle with 10, and Amber Group and Animoca Brands with 9 each.
John Kim

Round led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT and Axon Partners Group, and with participation from existing and new investors.
BARCELONA, Spain , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stark Future, the Barcelona company behind the world's best-selling enduro motorcycle, today announced the close of a financing round with a total transaction value in excess of €150 million, the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. The round values Stark Future at €1.2 billion pre-money, making it Europe's first electric motorcycle company valued above €1 billion. The round was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT climate private equity strategy and Spain-based international investment firm Axon Partners Group, with participation from existing shareholders and friends and family. The round was oversubscribed and exceeded the initial target, prompting the Company to keep the door open for a second closing to accommodate additional strategic partners, including Lombard Odier among others.
Continue Reading
Anton Wass - CEO and Founder of Stark Future
Stark Future HQ - Barcelona
Stark VARG SM_Lineup
Anton Wass, Production line Barcelona HQ
Founded in 2020 on an uncompromising belief that electric motorcycles should not just be the green alternative, but the better machine, Stark Future builds bikes designed to beat the best combustion competitors in every category they enter. Today, the VARG platform, spanning motocross, enduro and supermoto, is designed, engineered and built in-house at the Company's 20,000 m² facility on the outskirts of Barcelona. The new capital will fund global expansion and the development of new electric platforms.
In just three years of sales, Stark has gone from challenger to category leader. The VARG is now the best-selling enduro motorcycle on the planet, outselling every combustion competitor. Within its first year, Stark took around 50% of the enduro market in Germany and the top spot in France and Italy, while the United States has grown to be its largest market by volume. From a standing start, Stark has taken around 5% of the €3 billion global off-road motorcycle market from combustion in three years. The new capital is aimed at repeating that, and more, by entering new motorcycle categories, in a much larger €90 billion addressable motorcycle market. Few hardware companies grow this fast. Fewer do it profitably.
Anton Wass, Founder and CEO of Stark Future, says: "Six years ago, Stark was an unwavering belief that electric could be the better machine, not the compromise. Today it's the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. We turned the industry on its head once with the VARG, taking 5% of a €3 billion market from combustion in three years. This gives us the resources to do it again, and more, in a €90 billion market. articles.title: Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology
articles.snippet: Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology Robotics & Automation News
articles.text:
Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology
November 15, 2026 by Sam Francis
Venture capital firm Zacua Ventures has closed its second investment fund at $135 million, more than doubling the size of its original $56 million fund as it expands its focus on robotics, physical AI and technologies for industrial applications.
The San Francisco-based firm says Fund II was 35 percent oversubscribed, attracting commitments from more than 30 corporate and institutional investors across over 20 countries.
Originally focused on construction technology, Zacua is broadening its investment strategy to include manufacturing, energy, mining, infrastructure and other sectors it collectively describes as the “Physical Industries”.
The firm believes these sectors offer substantial opportunities for technologies that combine robotics, artificial intelligence and software with practical industrial expertise.
Vivin Hegde, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “The industries that underpin modern life are entering a forced transformation cycle. Housing is out of reach. Energy grids are under pressure. Workforces are aging out. The AI infrastructure buildout is placing even greater demands on the industries already struggling to keep pace.
“These are not isolated problems; they’re converging across the Physical Industries, a category venture capital has largely overlooked. We built Zacua in construction because we saw these challenges firsthand. Fund II takes what we learned there and applies it to the broader physical world.”
Building on construction robotics investments
Zacua has already invested in 34 early-stage companies across 11 markets, with several investments demonstrating its interest in industrial automation.
Among its portfolio companies is Gravis Robotics, an ETH Zurich spinout developing physical AI for autonomous construction equipment. The company raised $200 million in Series A funding from SoftBank earlier this year, reaching a reported valuation of $1 billion.
Another investment is Origin Robotics, whose OG1 robot autonomously finishes interior walls. The company emerged from stealth with $20 million in seed and Series A financing, with Zacua leading the latter round.
Other investments include Flexnode, which develops modular data centers, and CURA Climate, which is working on technologies to reduce emissions from cement production.
Zacua’s first exit came earlier this year when construction risk-management software company Document Crunch was acquired by Trimble.
Expanding industrial investment
Fund II’s investors include Volvo Group Venture Capital, Holcim Maqer Ventures, Hilti Venture, Trimble Ventures, Acciona, DPR Construction, Mortenson and Dubai Future District Fund.
The firm says its corporate investor network provides portfolio companies with access to industrial customers, technical expertise and opportunities to test emerging technologies in operational environments.
Juan Nieto, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “Fund I proved that our model works in one of the most complex and consequential industries in the world.
“Fund II allows us to take that same playbook much further. We are not changing what we do. We are applying the same early-stage conviction, founder-first philosophy and industry network across the broader Physical Industries.”

articles.title: Woodlands startup Mavria raises $130M to mass-produce AI data centers
articles.snippet: Woodlands startup Mavria raises $130M to mass-produce AI data centers InnovationMap

seed funding
Woodlands startup Mavria raises $130M to mass-produce AI data centers
John Egan
Nov 16, 2026, 11:30 am
Adam Blake, Nick Poradek and Seth Cohen founded Mavria this spring. Photo courtesy of Mavria
The Woodlands-based Mavria , which mass-produces factory-built modular AI data centers, just emerged from stealth mode with $130 million in funding at a $1 billion valuation.
Mavria raised the money in pre-seed and seed rounds led by Paradigm, an investment firm that concentrates on early-stage startups developing “pioneer” technology. Participants in the funding rounds include AMP PBC, Critical Frontier, Dream Ventures and Liquid 2 Ventures, co-founded by former NFL quarterback Joe Montana.
The company’s inaugural product, Terrain, is a prefabricated data center designed for AI labs, cloud computing providers and data center developers. Mavria says its platform avoids ground-up construction, delivering infrastructure more quickly and at a lower cost.
Mavria tells the Wall Street Journal that the first Terrain unit is being built at a Houston-area factory. The 5-megawatt Terrain system features power distribution, direct liquid cooling, controls and server racks.
“America sets the pace at the intelligence frontier. But the race is moving from the lab into the physical world,” Adam Blake, co-founder and CEO of Mavria, wrote in a blog post .
“Intelligence needs data centers. Data centers need power. Power needs factories, equipment, supply chains, and skilled workers, but much of that infrastructure is still built one custom project at a time, on timelines measured in years.”
Blake and Mavria’s two other co-founders, Nick Poradek and Seth Cohen, most recently worked at the U.S. Department of Energy. There, they focused on reforming the nuclear power sector.
From start to finish, it can take roughly three to six years to build a data center at an estimated cost of $10 million to $37 million per megawatt. Based on those figures, a 100-megawatt data center might cost as much as $3.7 billion.
Here are brief bios of Blake, Poradek and Cohen, who co-founded Mavria in May.
Adam Blake
Blake most recently was a senior advisor to U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright. He is co-founder and former CEO of Zego, a provider of energy management technology for property managers. Zego spun out from Brightergy, a commercial solar company. Blake is founder and former CEO of Brightergy.
Nick Poradek
Poradek , chief operating officer at Mavria, was also an advisor to the U.S. energy secretary. He is founder and former CEO of Spring-based Edera Energy, co-founder of The Woodlands-based craft-ice brand Clarity Ice, and founder and former CEO of The Woodlands-based Edera Capital. Poradek sold Edera Energy, a manufacturer of oilfield equipment, to Liberty Energy, a fracking company. Wright is Liberty’s founder and former chairman and CEO.
Seth Cohen
Cohen , chief strategy officer and chief legal officer at Mavria, was head of nuclear law and policy at the Department of Energy. He is also a former NASA advisor and a former attorney at Kirkland & Ellis.
“We believe in rapidly deploying infrastructure as a product, rather than custom-building every project,” Blake said. “We’re bringing together engineering, manufacturing, supply chains and capital so that every project makes us better at delivering the next.”
